newsitem.title: USA: Wallace holders turn down Wyser-Pratte plan.
newsitem.headline: Wallace holders turn down Wyser-Pratte plan.

text.p: Wallace Computer Services Inc said on Wednesday the director nominees and both bylaw proposals by Guy Wyser-Pratte were turned down by shareholders.

Based on final certified voting results delivered at Wednesday's reconvened annual meeting, Wallace said shareholders turned down bylaw proposals by Wyser-Pratte which would have limited the company's takeover defence.

Wallace Computer Chief Executive Officer Bob Cronin also said he estimated arbitrageurs held less than six percent of the company's shares. During the last takeover battle with Moore Corp Ltd in January, takeover speculators held an estimated 47 percent of Wallace stock, he said.
Cronin also said the company's share price has held up despite the pressure of a large arbitrage sell-off over the last 11 months.
Wallace shares were trading at 32-1/2, up 1/2.
Regarding the Wyser-Pratte proposals, the company said shareholders elected the board's nominees, Cronin, Richard Doyle and Neele Stearns, with each receiving at least 79.2 percent of the vote casts.
Wyser-Pratte and his two fellow nominees each received 17.2 percent of the votes cast, the company said.

Shareholders rejected a Wyser-Pratte proposal to opt out of Section 203 of the Delaware General Corp Law by more than a two to one margin, the company said. Section 203 provides anti-takeover or poison pill, defences for the company, which last year fended off an unsolicited bid from Moore.

They also turned down Wyser-Pratte's tender offer proposal, Wallace said. This proposal was aimed at getting Walace to drop all defences to a hostile offer after 90 days unless specifically approved by special shareholder vote.
Cronin said he believed that after the company's annual meeting adjourned on November 6, many of the remaining arbitrage positions, including Wyser-Pratte's, were sold.
Wyser-Pratte also withdrew a lawsuit he filed against the company in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, the company said.
